strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with local elementwise ops
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all_reduce(REDUCE_SUM) calls with interleaved local scaling/unscaling operations on full tensors between each collective. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches with full payload (W*S elements) each time. Represents the baseline reference approach with maximum dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused scale-reduce with pre-computed coefficients
strategies.desc: Pre-computes the cumulative effect of all 8 stages' scale/unscale operations into per-shard coefficients, then performs a single initial all-reduce followed by 7 all-reduces with fused local scaling before each collective. Reduces to 8 dispatches but fuses the scale/unscale arithmetic into the pre-collective computation to minimize memory traffic between compute and communication.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter plus all-gather pipeline
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing pipelining of the 8 stages where each rank can begin local computation on its assigned shard immediately after reduce-scatter completes. Increases dispatch count to 16 but enables overlap of computation with communication and reduces intermediate buffer sizes during the scatter phase.

strategies.name: Vectorized multi-shard local operations
strategies.desc: Restructures local scaling loops to operate on reshaped tensors enabling vectorized operations across multiple shards simultaneously, then performs standard all-reduce. Still requires 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead by batching shard-wise operations using tensor views and broadcasting instead of explicit loops over W shards.

strategies.name: Chunked all-reduce with interleaved computation
strategies.desc:
Splits each all-reduce into multiple smaller all-reduce operations on contiguous chunks of the tensor, interleaving local scale/unscale operations on already-reduced chunks while communication proceeds on remaining chunks. Increases dispatch count (8*C chunks) but enables better compute-communication overlap and improves cache locality for local operations on smaller working sets.
